noted_by.background:
Obviously this guy would have been hyped much earlier but since the 4th fight of his career he's been with ACA. After going 6-0 under a quality banner like that he decided to leave and pursue the UFC dream with his first step being a bit of a drop in competition but still picking up a regional title and an easy win.

He's unbelievably talented both standing and on the ground and in particular the way he showed Alexsandro Praia the right then blasted him with the left in ACA stands out as a kid who not only hits hard and quickly but is also intelligent in the way he sets things up.

Ideally the UFC will just sign him straight away but he might have to have a fight or two in a Fight Pass promotion like UAE Warriors to truly get on the radar but at 22 and already in double digit wins, time is on his side.

report.summary:
October's biggest change came from the list itself, not the cage: on Oct 6 the list moved to the top 100 per division, which cut it from 963 names to 676 in one rebuild, and the sweeps of 14 regional promotions then refilled it (112 new names since Oct 1, 96 of them newly eligible from this month's sweep, 15 from LFA alone). Because the list shrank, almost every rank number moved up without a fight, so read the moves by score change. Most of the 338 departures were squeezed out by the division cap; the rest aged past 28, had records the sources disagree on, or signed (Asaf Chopurov and Joel Faglier both debuted in the UFC).

The month's real jumps came with wins. Kristians Boguzs (+25, a win at KSW 122) and Murad Ibragimov (+26, over Juscelino Pantoja at UAE Warriors 74) made the biggest gains, followed by Elene Loladze at Rkena x PFL, Tulio Macena at Jungle Fight 156, and Ivan Lisogorov, Zafar Rashidov, Ikuya Akabane and Tsuyoshi Yoshida, each with a win. Two owner's picks reached the top 100: Khotam Boynazarov (#30) and Bektur Zhenishbek Uulu (#60, a decision win at ACA 209).

The falls came with losses: Mucahit Aydin (-25, beaten by Zurab Ivaniadze at Rkena x PFL), Jason Asher and Davi Cabral (both lost on the Contender Series), Jakob Dyrup at FCR 31, Zayne Havener to Jake Woodley at LFA 244, and Emil Musaev and Gabriel Urbino. Some moves had no fight behind them and came from the field (re-rated opponents and Fight Matrix's ranks): Giannis Kazantzidis rose from #307 to #79 and Magomed Kurbanov and Melany Gomez climbed, while Khalil Pirmagomedov, Nikolay Atanasov and Baissangour Chamsoudinov slid.
